the object.

At time t = 0 the object is at point X.
What is the displacement of the object from point X at time t = 0.80 s?
A
1.6 m
B
1.8 m
C
2.0 m
D
3.2 m

hints: Notice the $v$-$t$ graph starts at $v = -2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $t=0$ and crosses the $t$-axis at $t=0.20\text{ s}$, so part of the area is below the axis.
Recall displacement is the signed area under a $v$-$t$ graph, with area below the $t$-axis counted as negative and area above counted as positive.

Read $v$ at $t=0.80\text{ s}$ from the straight line, then calculate the small negative triangle from $0$ to $0.20\text{ s}$ and the larger positive triangle from $0.20\text{ s}$ to $0.80\text{ s}$ and add them with signs.
walkthrough: Identify what is given: $v = -2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $t=0$, the line crosses $v=0$ at $t=0.20\text{ s}$, and at $t=0.60\text{ s}$ the graph shows $v=4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
State the rule: displacement from X is the signed area under the $v$-$t$ graph from $t=0$ to $t=0.80\text{ s}$.
Find $v$ at $t=0.80\text{ s}$ by extending the uniform gradient: $v = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate the negative displacement from $t=0$ to $t=0.20\text{ s}$ as a triangle below the axis: $\Delta x_1 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.20\text{ s} \times (-2\text{ m s}^{-1}) = -0.20\text{ m}$.

Calculate the positive displacement from $t=0.20\text{ s}$ to $t=0.80\text{ s}$ as a triangle above the axis with base $0.60\text{ s}$ and height $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $\Delta x_2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.60\text{ s} \times 6\text{ m s}^{-1} = 1.8\text{ m}$.
Add with signs for net displacement: $\Delta x = -0.20\text{ m} + 1.8\text{ m} = 1.6\text{ m}$ with unit $\text{m}$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Net signed area from $t=0$ to $t=0.80\text{ s}$ is $-0.2\text{ m} + 1.8\text{ m} = 1.6\text{ m}$.

B.explanation: This is only the positive area from $t=0.20\text{ s}$ to $t=0.80\text{ s}$ and ignores the $-0.2\text{ m}$ displacement before the graph crosses zero.

C.explanation: This overestimates the net area, likely from misreading $v$ at $t=0.80\text{ s}$ or the time when $v=0$ on the $v$-$t$ grid.

D.explanation: This is about twice the correct value, from adding magnitudes of areas instead of subtracting the negative area below the $t$-axis.
